name: DynamicWebLab Form Notifications
author: Maidul

sections.description:
This plugin sends every Contact Form 7 submission to the chat app or tool your team already uses. Choose any mix of Telegram, Discord, Microsoft Teams, WhatsApp (Cloud API) and n8n, and get a message with the form’s fields shortly after a visitor sends the form.

It works with Contact Form 7 only. Other form plugins are not supported.

Use it when you want to:
* see new enquiries in a Telegram group or Discord channel
* send different forms to different channels (sales, support, HR)
* pass the full form data as JSON to n8n and connect it to a CRM or spreadsheet

Features

  • Telegram bot, Discord webhook, Microsoft Teams webhook, WhatsApp Cloud API and n8n webhook
  • Several services at once for the same form
  • Per-form routing and global defaults
  • Message templates for each service, with Contact Form 7 field tags such as [your-name] and [all_fields]
  • Test buttons to check a connection
  • History of sent and failed notifications, and a dashboard widget
  • Rate limit per minute to protect your accounts from spam
  • Translation ready

Before you use it

Visitors’ form data (names, emails, messages) is sent to the services you enable. See “External services”. A copy is kept in your site database; completed and failed items are deleted after 30 days.

External Services

This plugin connects to external APIs in order to send form submission notifications via WhatsApp, Telegram, Microsoft Teams, Discord, and N8N.

WhatsApp Cloud API (Meta/Facebook)
Used to send form submissions to WhatsApp recipients.
– Service URL: https://graph.facebook.com
– What is sent: The recipient’s phone number ID, access token, and message content derived from the submitted form fields.
– When: When a Contact Form 7 form is submitted.
– Terms of Service: https://www.facebook.com/legal/terms
– Privacy Policy: https://www.facebook.com/about/privacy

Telegram Bot API
Used to send form submissions to a Telegram chat via bot.
– Service URL: https://api.telegram.org
– What is sent: The bot token, chat ID, and message content derived from the submitted form fields.
– When: When a Contact Form 7 form is submitted.
– Terms of Service: https://core.telegram.org/terms
– Privacy Policy: https://telegram.org/privacy

Microsoft Teams Incoming Webhook
Used to send form submissions to Microsoft Teams channels.
– Service URL: https://webhook.office.com (or outlook.office.com, outlook.office365.com)
– What is sent: Message content derived from the submitted form fields.
– When: When a Contact Form 7 form is submitted (if configured).
– Terms of Service: https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/servicesagreement
– Privacy Policy: https://privacy.microsoft.com/en-us/privacystatement

Discord Webhook
Used to send form submissions to Discord channels via webhooks.
– Service URL: https://discord.com (or discordapp.com)
– What is sent: Message content derived from the submitted form fields, including embeds for formatted notifications.
– When: When a Contact Form 7 form is submitted (if configured).
– Terms of Service: https://discord.com/terms
– Privacy Policy: https://discord.com/privacy

N8N Automation (Self-Hosted or Cloud)
Used to send complete form data to N8N workflow webhooks for automation.
– Service URL: Your N8N instance URL (self-hosted or n8n.cloud)
– What is sent: Complete JSON payload including form ID, timestamp, site URL, and all form field data.
– When: When a Contact Form 7 form is submitted (if configured).
– Terms of Service: https://n8n.io/legal/self-serve-terms/ (if using n8n.cloud)
– Privacy Policy: https://n8n.io/legal/privacy (if using n8n.cloud)
– Note: Self-hosted N8N instances are under your control and privacy policy.

Data and requests
Visitors’ personal data from the form (the fields your message template includes) is sent to each service you enable. A copy of each submission is kept in your site’s database, and completed or failed items are deleted after 30 days. Requests to Telegram, WhatsApp, Microsoft Teams and Discord carry a User-Agent header that includes your site URL.

License

This plugin is licensed under the GPLv2 or later.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin files to the /wp-content/plugins/chat-notifications-for-telegram-with-cf7 directory, or install the plugin through the WordPress plugins screen directly.
  2. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ screen in WordPress.
  3. Navigate to Settings > DynamicWebLab Form Notifications to configure your WhatsApp, Telegram, Microsoft Teams, Discord, and N8N credentials.
sections.faq:
Which form plugins does it work with?

Contact Form 7 only.

Do I need WhatsApp Business?

Yes. WhatsApp uses Meta’s Cloud API and needs a verified Meta business account and an access token. Create an app in the Meta for Developers portal to get the credentials.

How do I get a Telegram bot token?

Create a bot with @BotFather in Telegram, copy the token into the Telegram tab, and add the chat ID.

How do I set up Discord?

Channel settings > Integrations > Webhooks > New webhook. Paste the URL into the Discord tab. Per-form overrides let you route specific forms to different channels.

Can one form go to several services?

Yes. Configure any combination; per-form routing lets you pick the destination per form.

Can I change the message?

Yes. Each service has a template that accepts your form’s field tags.

What data leaves my site?

The message text (or the full form data for n8n) goes to the services you configure over HTTPS. Do not send sensitive personal data to chat apps unless you have a reason and consent.

What is the difference between the chat services and n8n?

Chat services get a text message for people to read. n8n gets the full form data as JSON for automations.

Will this slow down my website?

Notifications are queued and sent in the background through WP-Cron, so visitors do not wait for them. The plugin adds no front-end scripts.
sections.changelog:
2.3.1

  • Compatibility: tested with WordPress 7.1.

2.3.0

  • Naming Update: Plugin renamed to “DynamicWebLab Form Notifications” to comply with WordPress.org naming guidelines
  • Fix: Updated N8N Terms of Service URL to correct endpoint
  • Fix: Updated “Tested up to” to WordPress 7.0 (major version only)

2.2.0

  • Discord Integration: Native Discord support with webhook URL configuration in its own tab

2.1.0

  • UI Overhaul: Redesigned settings page with sidebar + content layout, teal color scheme, and modern styling
  • New: SVG icon system with 37 inline icons replacing all emojis in the admin UI
  • New: External admin CSS file (assets/css/admin.css) — no inline styles in PHP
  • Improved: “How to” instruction sections rewritten with 3-card overviews, step-by-step guides, and color-coded notice boxes
  • Improved: Template editor emoji picker replaced with icon buttons with tooltip labels
  • Improved: Sticky save bar with blur backdrop at bottom of content area
  • Improved: Platform integration cards with gradient backgrounds and SVG icons

2.0.0

  • Major: Message Template Composer — Fully customizable message templates per platform (WhatsApp, Telegram, Teams). Use [field-name] tags to insert form values, [all_fields] to include all fields, and {if field}...{/if} conditional blocks.
  • New: Emoji picker built into the template editor for quick emoji insertion.
  • New: Available field tags panel — click to insert CF7 field tags into your template.
  • New: Conditional syntax support — show content only when a field has a value, with optional else blocks.
  • New: Test Message button for Telegram — validate your bot token and chat ID with one click.
  • New: Reset to Default template button per platform.
  • Tweak: Queue processor now renders per-platform messages using each platform’s own template.
  • Tweak: FormHooks uses TemplateEngine for default message generation.

1.5.0

  • Major: Rate Limiting — Throttle form submissions per minute to prevent API abuse from spam. Configurable limit (0–100) with per-form throttled status display.
  • New: RateLimiter class using the existing queue table for counting recent submissions — no new database tables.
  • New: Throttled forms shown in General tab with count/limit display and one-click reset.
  • New: chatnoticf7_rate_limited action fires when a form is throttled (allows custom handling).
  • Tweak: Rate limit capped at 100 per minute to prevent misconfiguration.

1.4.0

  • Major: Notification History Log — New “History” tab in settings showing all sent notifications with status, form ID, timestamp, message preview, and retry count.
  • New: Dashboard widget showing at-a-glance notification stats (sent, failed, queued) with recent activity feed.
  • New: History table with status and form ID filters, paginated with previous/next navigation.
  • New: Automatic daily purge of completed/failed items older than 30 days.
  • Tweak: Successful queue items now marked as completed instead of deleted, enabling the history log.

1.3.0

  • Major: Visual Per-Form Routing Table — Replaced the raw textarea with a proper interactive table UI. Each row has a CF7 form dropdown and per-platform input fields with add/remove controls.
  • New: JavaScript-powered dynamic row management — add and remove form overrides without page reload.
  • New: Form dropdowns automatically disable already-assigned forms to prevent duplicate routing.
  • New: chatnoticf7_overrides_json option storing overrides in standardized JSON format alongside the existing parsed array.
  • Tweak: Raw textarea fallback preserved for backward compatibility.

1.2.0

  • Security: Removed error_log() calls from queue processor — API error responses could theoretically leak service internals. Replaced with do_action hooks so developers can opt-in to custom logging.
  • Performance: Set autoload=false on all plugin options — credentials and settings are no longer loaded on every WordPress page request. Existing installations are migrated automatically on upgrade.
  • Tweak: Added chatnoticf7_queue_*_result action hooks for each notifier in the queue processor, passing the result array, queue item ID, and form ID.

1.1.0

  • Major: Async Notification Queue — Form submissions no longer block the user. Notifications are queued and processed in the background via WP-Cron, eliminating the 37-second timeout ceiling.
  • New: Custom DB table for the notification queue with automatic retry (3 attempts) and stale-job recovery.
  • New: Automatic queue processing via wp_schedule_single_event() — works with both WP-Cron and system cron.
  • New: Proper plugin activation (table creation) and uninstall (table cleanup) hooks.
  • Tweak: Unused $form_id variable cleanup in sanitize_form_specific_settings.

1.0.4

  • Critical Fix: Replaced wp_safe_remote_post() with wp_remote_post() across all notifiers to prevent external API calls (WhatsApp, Telegram, Teams) from being silently blocked by WordPress safe host validation
  • Bug Fix: Fixed dash (-) fallthrough in per-form overrides — using - now correctly falls back to global settings instead of overriding with a literal dash
  • Security Fix: Added HTTPS scheme validation for N8N webhook URLs to prevent SSRF attacks
  • Security Fix: N8N notifier now validates webhook URLs before sending requests
  • Tweak: Settings page textarea now renders from the raw stored value, preserving user formatting and dash placeholders
  • Tweak: Updated WordPress tested-up-to to 6.8

1.0.3

  • Major UI/UX Overhaul:
    • Complete settings page redesign with modern, beautiful interface
    • Enhanced tab navigation with smooth transitions and gradient backgrounds
    • Improved form inputs with better focus states and hover effects
    • Added gradient buttons with lift animations for better interactivity
    • Enhanced card styling with hover effects and better shadows
    • Improved responsive design for mobile and tablet devices
    • Better typography and spacing throughout the admin interface
  • Comprehensive Documentation Added:
    • WhatsApp: Step-by-step Meta Developer setup guide
    • Telegram: Complete bot creation and Chat ID instructions
    • Microsoft Teams: Incoming Webhook configuration guide
    • N8N: Workflow setup and JSON payload documentation
    • Per-Form Overrides: Detailed routing examples and format guide
    • Integrations Tab: Beautiful overview of all active integrations
  • Bug Fixes:
    • Fixed critical WhatsApp option name bug preventing notifications
    • Fixed text domain typos for proper translation support
    • Fixed empty ID attribute in form selector dropdown
    • Fixed Telegram legacy Markdown escaping bug
  • Readme Updates:
    • Added N8N automation documentation
    • Updated feature list to include all 4 integrations
    • Added external services disclosure for N8N
    • Improved plugin description and tags
    • Added FAQ about future form plugin support (WPForms, Fluent Forms, etc.)
    • Added FAQ explaining N8N vs messaging platforms
  • Roadmap Updates:
    • Comprehensive plan for supporting WPForms, Fluent Forms, Formidable Forms, Gravity Forms
    • Implementation strategy for multi-form-builder support
    • Technical architecture planning for universal form integration

1.0.2

  • Added Microsoft Teams integration via Incoming Webhook
  • Made the default “New Contact Form 7 submission” message translatable
  • Improved WhatsApp notifier with error handling, validation, and extensible hooks
  • Added per-form override support for Microsoft Teams
  • Updated readme description for better SEO and keyword targeting
  • Fixed critical WhatsApp option name bug preventing notifications

1.0.1

  • Improved Telegram notifier with error handling, message sanitization, and logging
  • Added return values for send_message() to allow success/failure detection
  • Implemented safer MarkdownV2 escaping for Telegram messages
  • Added hooks and filters for payload customization and parse mode

1.0.0

  • Initial release with basic WhatsApp and Telegram integration
